title: First Hellenic Republic
capsule: The First Hellenic Republic (formally proclaimed 1 January 1822 at Epidaurus during the Greek War of Independence) encompassed the revolutionary Greek state that fought Ottoman rule and was internationally recognized as a kingdom in 1832. Ioannis Kapodistrias served as the first Governor (1827–1831) and was assassinated at Nauplia; factional strife followed until the Great Powers imposed a monarchy under the Bavarian prince Otto. The republican designation in historiography is contested since the state functioned as various constitutional forms; the from/to span here reflects the revolutionary period through the consolidation of the monarchy.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The effective territory of the revolutionary Greek state expanded continuously during 1821–1832 and was never fixed; mapping any single boundary is an approximation of a polity whose control was highly contested at every point.
